Done. All 17 tests in `markdown_test.go` pass, and `go vet` is clean. ## What I did Per the spec in `.docs/instructions.md`, I rewrote `markdown.go` from a byte-at-a-time state machine into a line-oriented renderer. The original tracked `pos` by hand, mutated the input string, and used several opaque tricks — an `he` ("header encountered") flag that was never reset, a `LastIndex` comparison to detect a paragraph after a list, and a `strings.Contains(markdown, "\n")` guard on list items. The rewrite splits the work into three small, named pieces: - **`Render`** — splits the document into lines and renders each as a header, list item, or paragraph. A `
    ` opens on the first `*` line and closes when a non-list line appears or input ends — which replaces both the `LastIndex` hack and the trailing `switch`/`strings.Contains(html, "

    ")` logic in one obvious place. - **`renderHeader`** — counts leading `#`s: 1–6 become `

    `–`

    ` (consuming the one space after the markers), 7+ fall back to a paragraph with the `#`s left in place. Mid-line `#`/`*` are naturally literal since only line prefixes are interpreted. - **`applyEmphasis`** + **`replaceFirst`** — one subtlety I initially got wrong: the original uses `strings.Replace(..., 1)`, so it substitutes exactly *one* pair of `__` and one pair of `_` (first occurrence opens, next closes), not all pairs. My first attempt with `ReplaceAll` failed the emphasis tests; the fix preserves the original single-pair semantics exactly, with `__` handled before `_` so bold isn't misread as paired italics. Refactoring notes are included as comments, as the spec suggested. No other files were touched.
